# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm gen`. Edit the config schema or secret metadata instead. -->

`config.yaml` is validated by the [JSON Schema](../packages/contracts/config.schema.json). Paths below use `[]` for array entries. Required means required in that object; defaults may fill optional fields.

The JSON Schema cannot express every cross-field rule. Run `board doctor --offline` after editing the file.

## Spur UI session links

`web.spurUiOrigin` is the optional Spur UI origin, independent of the Board web listener. The intended session link URL is `<origin>/sessions/<session id>`; when unset, the fallback is plain session IDs. Run `board doctor --json` to check reachability: `web.spurUiOrigin` warns when unset, passes on any HTTP response from the origin root, and only warns on transport errors or a short timeout; UI problems never block readiness or updates. HTTP UI origins work on any host without voice, while web.publicOrigin keeps HTTP loopback-only. Start the Spur UI or fix the origin, proxy or TLS configuration, then restart the daemon after config changes and rerun doctor. This checks the origin, not individual session pages.

Running checks, or no checks yet, hold a task only at the exit of this column. Red checks return the task to Dev from any column; a task whose turn is taken returns right after that turn's submit. A task enters ready-to-merge only with green checks. With dev, a cancelled check is red at once. With another column, a cancelled check counts as running until two complete GitHub polls after the one that saw it, about two GitHub poll intervals, and then counts as red; a new run in that window replaces it, and a source whose polls stay incomplete keeps it running. The daemon reads the key at start, so a change takes effect after a restart.             |

It is not necessarily the maintainer's own account: when agents push as one account and a maintainer approves as another, set the agents' account, or no PR is discovered. Comments, reviews and approvals by this login or by a bot (GitHub App) are not external: they never return a task to Dev, approve External Review or block its approval. ## Example: green checks at External Review

`projects[].checksGate` moves the wait for running checks from Dev to an enabled column right of it. With `external-review`, a task with running checks passes Dev, Review and Product Review and waits at External Review's exit; red checks still return it to Dev from any column, and Ready to Merge needs green checks. Only under a column other than `dev` a cancelled check counts as running for two complete GitHub polls after the one that saw it, about two GitHub poll intervals; with `dev` it is red at once. The daemon reads the key at start, so a change takes effect after a restart.

```yaml
projects:
  - id: web
    tracker:
      type: github-issues
      repo: example-org/web
    repos: [example-org/web]
    operatorGithubLogin: octocat
    columns:
      - id: todo
      - id: dev
      - id: review
      - id: external-review
      - id: ready-to-merge
      - id: done
    checksGate: external-review
operator:
  slack: U0000000000
digest:
  tz: UTC
```

## Example: follow the GitHub review rule at External Review

`approvalRule: github-rules` on the `external-review` column makes a task leave External Review only when a reviewer other than `operatorGithubLogin` approved, nobody requested changes (GitHub's review decision or a reviewer's latest review), and the Board stored a decision for the PR head that GitHub's review rule is satisfied: a required check completed, or, when none is required, every check except skipped ones green and at least one (no checks at all also counts); and the merge state clean, unstable or with hooks. The rule is read from the base branch's branch protection and rulesets on each full PR read; when several projects poll the repo with the key, the newest read of the rule for the head counts for each of them, while each keeps its own decision. Only GitHub's answer changes the stored decision: a merge state clean, unstable or with hooks stores satisfied, and blocked with every required check completed stores a block, read as `unresolved_threads` while review threads stay unresolved and as `review_rule_blocked` otherwise. Every other read keeps the stored decision and holds the task where it is: a required check, one GitHub marks required or a context the rule lists, that is pending or missing waits as `checks_pending` unless the merge state is clean, unstable or with hooks (a listed context counts only through a run GitHub marks required, from branch protection and rulesets alike, so a run of that name from an app the branch does not require leaves it missing); a base branch rule the token cannot read, or one with more than 100 ruleset rules, waits as `review_rule_unreadable`; a merge state GitHub has not computed, behind, or a head with no decision waits as `merge_state_unknown`. GitHub's review decision requesting changes counts once the merge state is computed; a reviewer's latest review always counts. A new head starts without a decision, and once a head with no decision has stayed undecided for 30 minutes, time outside External Review included, with its merge state unknown or behind or its rule unreadable and no changes requested, GitHub's review decision on an unknown merge state included, the operator gets one item while the task is in External Review. A draft and a conflict still return the task to Dev. `board doctor` prints the rule it reads as `github.review_rule`. Without the key, or with `any-approval`, one approval by a reviewer other than `operatorGithubLogin` is enough while no such reviewer has requested changes. Remove the key before `board rollback` to a version without it.

```yaml
projects:
  - id: web
    tracker:
      type: github-issues
      repo: example-org/web
    repos: [example-org/web]
    operatorGithubLogin: octocat
    columns:
      - id: todo
      - id: dev
      - id: review
      - id: external-review
        approvalRule: github-rules
      - id: ready-to-merge
      - id: done
operator:
  slack: U0000000000
digest:
  tz: UTC
```

## Example: mirror a GitHub Project status to Ready for Dev

`source` with `type: tracker` on the `ready-for-dev` column of a `github-issues` project makes the board place tasks between `todo` and `ready-for-dev` from a single-select field of a GitHub Project, such as Status = Ready. On every poll the board reads the Project, the field and its options, and the Project items of every open issue of `tracker.repo`, in one GraphQL request of about one rate-limit point; it never lists the items of the Project. An idle task in `todo` whose issue has the value moves to `ready-for-dev`; an idle task in `ready-for-dev` whose issue has another value, no value, has left the Project or is archived there moves back to `todo`. Each move is journaled as `task_mirror_moved`. In dispatcher shadow mode a shadow column in `todo` or `ready-for-dev` follows the same read even when the real column is already right, so a `--correct` of the shadow column does not outlast the next read; that shadow-only move keeps the visit and the turns of the real column, and its event carries `shadow: true`. A shadow column in `triage` or right of `ready-for-dev` stays. A task with an open PR or a live worker, a task in `triage`, and every column right of `ready-for-dev` are never touched. Manual moves into or out of `ready-for-dev` are refused with `column_mirrored`: change the status in the Project instead; `board move --correct` still works, and the next read applies the Project again. `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs the `read:project` scope (a fine-grained token: Projects read access for the Project owner). Only a complete read moves tasks: a failed or incomplete read freezes every position and reports one of the codes `mirror_project_forbidden`, `mirror_field_not_found`, `mirror_snapshot_incomplete`, `mirror_rate_limited` or `mirror_read_failed` (see `docs/errors.md`) on the `github-project` source until the next complete read. The mirror source pauses for budget at twice `github.reserveRemaining`, before the PR sources. `board doctor` checks the Project, the field and the option as `github.mirror`. Without the key, or with `source: manual`, the column is placed by hand as before. Remove the key before `board rollback` to a version without it.

```yaml
projects:
  - id: web
    tracker:
      type: github-issues
      repo: example-org/web
    repos: [example-org/web]
    operatorGithubLogin: octocat
    columns:
      - id: todo
      - id: triage
      - id: ready-for-dev
        source:
          type: tracker
          project: example-org/3
          field: Status
          value: Ready
      - id: dev
      - id: review
      - id: ready-to-merge
      - id: done
operator:
  slack: U0000000000
digest:
  tz: UTC
```

## Example: watch what changed after an approval

`projects[].approvalWatch` names the top-level directories (`back/`) and root files (`package.json`) whose change after an approval matters for the project. For each open PR, `board status --json` lists `prSummary[].approvals[]` and `board task <key> --json` lists `links[].approvals[]`: one entry per latest approval with its `author`, `sha` and `onHead`. For an approval on an older commit, `commitsAfter` counts the commits after it up to the head, `changedAfter` lists every top-level entry they changed (`name/` for a directory, a bare name for a root file), and `watchedAfter` keeps the entries that match `approvalWatch`; a trailing `/` in either is ignored, so `back` and `back/` each match a directory or a file named `back`. Without the key every changed entry counts as watched. Merge commits, base-branch merges included, add neither commits nor entries. `notCounted` replaces the three fields when the commits cannot be counted: `history_rewritten` when the approved commit is no longer in the head history (a rebase or force-push), `rate_limit` while the GitHub budget is low, read again once it recovers, and `pr_too_large` above 100 commits. An entry without these fields is not read yet. It is a hint only: no gate, move or turn reads it. The daemon reads the key at start, so a change takes effect after a restart. Remove the key before `board rollback` to a version without it.

```yaml
projects:
  - id: web
    tracker:
      type: github-issues
      repo: example-org/web
    repos: [example-org/web]
    operatorGithubLogin: octocat
    approvalWatch: [back/, front/, package.json]
operator:
  slack: U0000000000
digest:
  tz: UTC
```

## Orchestrator projects

Use `role: orchestrator` for dedicated Spur projects that execute columns. Multiple orchestrators may belong to one board project. A named column executor must have role orchestrator or curator; the literals `operator` and `none` retain their meaning. Orchestrators have authority only for their assigned columns, without operator authority.

Board-wide bindings: list a Spur project in top-level `spurProjects` to serve every board project at once. `role: orchestrator` with `columns` fills each listed column that a board project enables and leaves at `none`; `role: operator` becomes the operator of each board project that lists no operator of its own. A project-level binding wins for its own project: a column orchestrator other than `none` (including `operator`) is kept, and a project's own operator replaces the board-wide one there. A project's own operator acts only in its project. Operator commands that name no project run for the operator token, the board-wide operator, or, without one, the operator of a one-project board. Such a Spur project is listed nowhere under `projects[].spurProjects`; one of its sessions acts on the turns, inbox, questions and doorbells of every board project it serves. A top-level `shortName` is unique across the board. An orchestrators-channel message without a known `@<shortName>` goes to `slack.defaultAddressee`; without it, to the board-wide operator; without one, when any shortName is set, to the operator of the first board project that lists one.

Breaking configuration change: change a dedicated worker column executor to `role: orchestrator`. For operator execution use the literal `orchestrator: operator`, rather than the name of an operator project. Curator executors remain supported. After an accepted session observation, existing worker links of a project changed to orchestrator are demoted to other, preserving link identity, bans and history. Known orchestrator sessions also link as other through explicit labels and manual links; sessions whose identity is unknown retain the existing manual behavior until observed.

## Session links

The Board links a Spur session to a task by three rules, tried in this order on every Spur poll. The first rule that names a task wins, except that a pull request match off the PR's head branch waits for the branch rule.

1. Explicit label. The session's Spur link `board-worker` is read first, then `board-other`; the first whose URL parses names the task. `board-worker` links the session as worker (other for a known orchestrator), `board-other` as other. The URL is `<Jira base>/browse/KEY-12` for a Jira task or `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/12` for a GitHub Issues task, with owner and repo spelled letter for letter as in `tracker.repo`, and with no trailing slash, query or fragment. A label that parses but names a task the Board does not track links nothing and turns off the next two rules for that session.
2. Pull request. The session's `pr` link is a PR linked to the task, and the session's Spur project is listed in that project's `spurProjects` with `role: worker`. When the session's branch equals that PR's head branch, this rule names the task. When it differs, or the Board has no head branch for the PR yet, the branch rule runs first; only if it names no task does the session link to the PR's task, always as other.
3. Branch. The session's Spur project is listed with `role: worker`, and its branch contains the task key in any letter case, not after a letter or digit and not before a digit (`WEBDEV-56` is not found in `XWEBDEV-56` or `WEBDEV-5698`), or equals the head branch of a PR linked to the task. Exactly one task must match. Sessions that share a branch in one poll stay unlinked unless the task already has a worker.

Scope: a `board-worker` or `board-other` label links a session from any Spur project. The pull request and branch rules need the session's Spur project listed in that project's `spurProjects` with `role: worker`. A worker still needs its Spur project in `spurProjects`, with any role, to call `board task`, `board ask` and `board comment`.

Roles: a session links to a task once, and that link keeps its first role except for orchestrator demotion described above. A session linked by the branch rule, or by the pull request rule on the PR's head branch, becomes worker when the task has no worker, otherwise other. A session linked by the pull request rule off the PR's head branch is always other. After `board unlink` removes a session, no automatic rule links it to that task again; `board link` restores it with its original role.

For a GitHub Issues task, a PR in `tracker.repo` links to its issue through `link.sources`, and PR discovery keeps only PRs whose author is `operatorGithubLogin`. Until that PR is linked, a session with an ordinary branch name links only through an explicit label.

Setting the label: `spur spawn` cannot set links. Set it on the new session with `spur slots --session <id> --link board-worker=<url>`; inside the session, `$SPUR_SESSION` holds its ID. Build the URL from the task key: `o/r#12` is `https://github.com/o/r/issues/12`.

Operator fallback: `board link <task> --session <session> --reason <value> --key <key>` links the session as worker when the task has none, otherwise as other; a known orchestrator always links as other.

Reviewers: a session of a `role: worker` Spur project whose `pr` link is a PR it only reviews, on a branch other than the PR's head, links to that PR's task by the pull request rule as other, even when the task has no worker. A review session checked out on the PR's head branch links as worker when the task has none, unless it sets `board-other` to the task's URL before its `pr` link appears. A later label changes nothing, because a link keeps its first role; the operator then removes the link with `board unlink <task> --session <session> --reason <value> --key <key>`. No automatic rule links it to that task again; `board link` restores it with its original role.

## secrets.env keys

Keep `secrets.env` private with mode `0600`. It lives beside `config.yaml` in the Board config directory, or under `BOARD_HOME` when set. Never put secret values in `config.yaml` or logs.

| Key                      | Required when | Purpose                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN`           | always        | Read GitHub repositories and check runs; also read:project when a ready-for-dev column mirrors a GitHub Project. |
| `JIRA_EMAIL`             | jira          | Jira account email.                                                                                              |
| `JIRA_API_TOKEN`         | jira          | Jira API token.                                                                                                  |
| `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`        | slack         | Slack bot Web API token.                                                                                         |
| `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`        | slack         | Slack app-level Socket Mode token.                                                                               |
| `SLACK_APP_CONFIG_TOKEN` | optional      | Verify the installed slash command through the Slack app manifest API.                                           |
| `SLACK_API_URL`          | optional      | Override the Slack API URL for local testing. https:, or http: only on a loopback host.                          |
